description:
THE actual nuclear part of this project. Replaces a fired furnace with a heat exchanger whose hot side is reactor helium.

SCOPE: a unit operation taking helium inlet temperature, pressure and mass flow on the hot side and a process stream on the cold side, returning duty and both outlet states, with a real pinch check so the model cannot silently transfer heat up a temperature gradient. Reuse the LMTD and NTU algebra already in dwsim-libs heat_exchanger; helium properties come from crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop (full Helmholtz EOS plus real transport correlations, already tested).

SAFETY-RELEVANT MODELLING NOTE for the docs: a real coupling would need an intermediate loop and tritium-permeation and pressure-boundary considerations between reactor and hydrocarbon process. This is an offline demonstration and models none of that. State that limitation explicitly rather than implying a deployable design.

Blocks on the scope decision (op-1z3o.1) and on a heat source existing at all.
title: refinery: nuclear process heater — the helium-to-process coupling unit operation

design:
Child epic of the integrated petrochemical and polymer platform (bn op-9941 / see #77 programme).

**Fidelity target: Engineering model (infrastructure)**

**A reusable framework — not separate mathematical infrastructure for PE, PP,
PS, PVC and PET.**

Reaction classes: initiation; propagation; termination; chain transfer;
branching; copolymerization; catalyst-site kinetics.

Different polymer technologies instantiate different subsets. That is the test
of whether the abstraction is right: if adding PP requires new machinery rather
than new parameters and a different subset of classes, it is wrong.

**Investigate literature-supported models and validation data before selecting
equations.** Kinetics chosen without a validation target cannot be checked, and
polymer kinetics has enough free parameters to fit anything.

Depends on the generic polymer representation and the existing reaction
infrastructure.


## Programme constraints

No monolithic plant solvers. Reuse existing reaction/thermo/separation infrastructure. Conservation preserved across every representation change. Do not push to `main`.
title: Petchem: Polymerization kinetics framework

description:
cargo +nightly doc -p outram-foam-basic-lib --no-deps emits 153 warnings, all pre-existing and none from fv_options. Breakdown measured 2026-08-05: 135 unresolved intra-doc links, 8 'X is both a function and a module' ambiguities (conjugate_gradient, gamg, gauss_seidel — each exists as both, so the links need a disambiguating prefix such as [`fn@conjugate_gradient`]), 6 public docs linking to private items (Ilu0Preconditioner -> ILU_PIVOT_FLOOR, gamg -> GamgCycle::solve_level, gamg -> prolong_field), and 4 redundant explicit link targets.

Broken intra-doc links are a direct hit on the workspace's 'human interface layer' rule: a reader hovering in rust-analyzer or browsing the rustdoc gets a dead link instead of the type they need. They also degrade the generated docs/api.md mirror.

For calibration, the equivalent sweep on outram-park-fork-offbeat took one pass and cleared 18 -> 0. The dominant fix there was a module carrying BOTH an outer /// doc at its declaration site and an inner //! doc in its file — rustdoc joins them and resolves links in the PARENT module's scope, so every link to a child item fails. Check for that pattern first here; it is likely responsible for a large share of the 135.

description:
The third HTGR-specific accident sequence, and the prerequisite for the other two: a break has to be characterised before you can say how much air or water enters through it.

THE PHYSICS. Helium at 3.0 MPa discharging to a ventilated confinement at atmospheric pressure is deeply choked (critical pressure ratio for a monatomic gas, gamma = 5/3, is about 0.487, so any downstream pressure below ~1.46 MPa gives sonic flow). Blowdown rate sets the depressurisation timescale, which sets when natural circulation can establish and therefore when air ingress begins. The PBMR-400 benchmark distinguishes PRESSURISED from DEPRESSURISED loss of forced cooling precisely because the two give very different core temperatures.

THE PAYOFF THE MAINTAINER IDENTIFIED. crates/tampines already has a critical_flow module. CAUTION: bead op-bcg records that its documentation CLAIMS Marviken validation THAT DOES NOT EXIST. So the critical-flow solver is a real asset but an unvalidated one, and op-bcg must be resolved before any depressurisation result is quoted. Marviken is a steam/water critical-flow test series in any case; a helium blowdown is a single-phase compressible gas problem and needs its own verification, most naturally against the analytical choked-flow solution for an ideal monatomic gas before moving to real-gas helium from outram-park-fork-coolprop.

SEQUENCING: verify choked flow analytically -> depressurisation transient -> then the air-ingress and steam-ingress beads, which both depend on knowing the break flow.

Also relates to op-1z3o.12 (pressure-flow network solve for the refinery dynamic mode) — both need flow driven by pressure difference rather than specified, so the formulations should be consistent even though the fluids differ.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
CORRECTION 2026-08-11 — this bead understated existing progress. Maintainer: 'while marviken validation is not done, edwards is.'

VERIFIED IN CODE. Edwards-O'Brien pipe blowdown IS implemented and tested in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/ (not in critical_flow/). tests.rs records the actual case inputs — initial enthalpy h = 9.857170e5 J/kg, pipe L = 4.096 m, D = 0.073 m, horizontal — and geometry.rs and drift_flux.rs carry Edwards-specific doc comments in the V&V style. So depressurisation-transient capability is NOT starting from zero.

WHAT op-bcg ACTUALLY SAYS, restated precisely so the two are not conflated: the false claim is in crates/tampines/src/critical_flow/, whose docs reference Moody / Zaloudek / Marviken data. Marviken is not done. Edwards is. Those are different modules and different benchmarks — do not treat op-bcg as invalidating the Edwards work.

THE REMAINING GAP FOR THIS BEAD IS STILL REAL, AND IT IS A FLUID-PHYSICS GAP, NOT A MISSING-CODE GAP. Edwards-O'Brien is a FLASHING TWO-PHASE WATER blowdown: subcooled water depressurises, flashes, and the choking is two-phase. An HTR-10 primary depressurisation is SINGLE-PHASE COMPRESSIBLE HELIUM. The drift-flux machinery Edwards validates is not the machinery a helium blowdown needs.

So the sequencing stands but the starting point is better than written:
1. Verify single-phase compressible choked flow analytically for an ideal monatomic gas (gamma = 5/3, critical pressure ratio ~0.487), which is a closed-form check.
2. Move to real-gas helium properties from outram-park-fork-coolprop.
3. Then the depressurisation transient.
The Edwards work gives a validated transient-blowdown framework to build within; it does not give helium choking for free.

title: HTR-10 accident: primary depressurisation and choked flow

description:
tsl-HinH2O.leapr is the only registered deck with nss>0 (nss=1, b7=1 free-gas O, aws=15.85751, sps=3.7939, mss=1). generate_tape refuses it via LeaprDeck::unsupported_features, so light-water S(a,b) cannot be regenerated at all.

Fortran oracle (NJOY2016 leapr.f90, commit ac5adf5f): for b7>0 the scatterer loop runs ONCE (line 398 'if (nss.eq.0.or.b7.gt.zero.or.isecs.gt.0) idone=1'), the ssm merge is skipped (3018 requires b7.le.zero), dwpix takes the normal principal /awr path (3035), and no secondary Teff table is written (3578 requires b7.le.zero). The ONLY difference from a single-scatterer deck is the MT=4 LIST head: NI=6*(nss+1)=12 (3307), NS=nss (3308), B(7)=b7, B(8)=mss*sps, B(9)=aws, B(10)=B(11)=0, B(12)=mss (3315-3321).

Scope: emit those constants in endout, thread the deck card-6 fields through generate_tape, and narrow the unsupported_features gate from 'nss!=0' to 'nss!=0 && b7<=0'.
title: njoy leapr: secondary-scatterer (nss>0, b7>0) support so H-in-H2O generates from its deck

description:
Observed once, 2026-08-11 ~15:16 SGT, on develop.

WHAT HAPPENED, exactly:
  $ ./scripts/push-beads-store.sh
  warning: could not push beads store ref to origin; beads remain local only

Immediately afterwards, by hand:
  $ git push origin refs/heads/beads/store:refs/heads/beads/store
  Everything up-to-date
  $ git rev-parse refs/heads/beads/store
  4beb401e2abc278df219140a944edc7d60eacbfe
  $ git ls-remote origin refs/heads/beads/store
  4beb401e2abc278df219140a944edc7d60eacbfe  refs/heads/beads/store
  $ git show refs/heads/beads/store:state.jsonl | grep -c op-nik1
  1

So the ref WAS published, including the bead created minutes earlier — the warning was false. No beads were actually stranded.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the whole point of the Stop-hook carve-out is that beads filed in a session are never left on one machine. A warning that cries wolf trains the reader to ignore the one time it is real.

SUSPECTED CAUSE, not confirmed: the script compares `git rev-parse` against `git ls-remote` and only pushes on a mismatch. Two plausible races, both consistent with what was seen — (a) the kopi-beans daemon was mid-flush, so local_sha moved between the rev-parse and the push; (b) a concurrent push (the Stop hook firing alongside the manual invocation) held the ref lock, so `git push` exited nonzero even though the ref reached origin. `git push` output is sent to /dev/null, so there is no evidence either way.

SUGGESTED FIX: capture the push's stderr instead of discarding it and include it in the warning, and re-check `git ls-remote` before warning — if the remote now matches the local ref, the push effectively succeeded and the warning should not fire. Do not silence the warning outright; make it accurate.
title: scripts/push-beads-store.sh printed a false 'beads remain local only' warning
